newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-SECOND-SEED IVANISEVIC BEATEN BY MARTIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SECOND-SEED IVANISEVIC BEATEN BY MARTIN.

text.p: American Todd Martin ended Goran Ivanisevic's hopes at the $800,000 CA Trophy on Friday when he beat the second-seeded Croatian 4-6 6-3 6-3.
In the semifinals, Martin will meet fifth-seeded Boris Becker, who despite a recurring wrist injury knocked out Switzerland's Marc Rosset 7-6 7-5.
Saturday's other semifinal on the indoor hardcourt will be contested by Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch and Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands.
Boetsch caused the day's other upset, beating third-seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov 7-6 7-6 to deny the Russian a chance of claiming his fifth title of the year.
Siemerink eliminated sentimental favourite Stefan Edberg 5-7 7-5 7-6 to deny the 30-year-old Swede a chance of winning one more title before his retirement at the end of the year.
Seventh-seeded Martin dropped serve at 3-4 to lose the first set 4-6, before stepping up a gear and hammering down the aces to claim the second and third sets with a breaks for 5-3 and 3-2.
Martin is aiming for his second title of the year, although he also reached the final at Memphis and semifinals at Wimbledon, Indianapolis and Toronto.

Unseeded Boetsch won both sets of a tight but bland match in tiebreaks, the first by 7-5 and the second by 7-2, to reverse last week's result when he was defeated by the world number four and French Open champion in the final at Lyon.
Edberg was weakened by a bout of flu which forced him to pull out of Lyon and started showing signs of fatigue after taking the first set.
Edberg, who will contest tournaments at Stuttgart, Paris and Stockholm before his retirement as well playing in the Davis Cup final, said: "It was a real pity that I lost today.
"This would have been a good opportunity to go for a last title before I quit. It was a close match today and I could have won."
Becker, who was forced to take a longer break than expected following a wrist injury sustained at Wimbledon, was pleased with his showing against Rosset.

"I'm happy because this is the first time in four months I've played three matches in a row," said the three-times Wimbledon champion, who lost in the first round in Bucharest, the second in Basle and pulled out of Lyon.
"The more I play the less afraid I am of my wrist and the better I play. But there are certain shots I still can't take," said Becker.
